prompt: A classmate claims "every quadrilateral with four equal sides is a square." You draw a rhombus that is squished flat and show it to her. What is the name for a single example that proves a general statement false?
hint: The word starts with "counter," as in something that counters a claim.

hints.text: The word starts with "counter," as in something that counters a claim.
It is one example that runs counter to the statement.

explanation: A counterexample is a single case that satisfies the hypothesis but not the conclusion.
The squished rhombus has four equal sides (hypothesis ✓) but is not a square (conclusion ✗).
One counterexample is enough to prove a general statement false — while no number of examples can prove one true.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why one is enough
steps: A statement that says "every" is making a promise about all cases.
Break the promise once and the statement is dead. That single broken case is the counterexample.
